ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a simple circuit, composed of a resistor $R$, a capacitor $C$, and an ideal battery connected in series. It is known that the circuit is powered on at time $t=0$, the voltage across the capacitor is $V_C(0)=0$, and the electromotive force of the battery is $\mathcal{E}$. Find the law of variation of the voltage $V_C(t)$ across the capacitor with time $t$.

Reasoning: The top is an aldehyde group and the total number of carbons is 6, so this compound is an aldohexose. The OH of the lowest chiral carbon C5 is on the right side, so it belongs to a D-sugar. Among D-aldohexoses, the structure with OH arranged as right-left-right-right corresponds to D-glucose. The question stem text is inconsistent with the image/specified method, but judging according to the specified method and the image, the answer is D-glucose.

method.method_draft: First describe the displayed Fischer projection. Count the carbon chain: aldehyde carbon at top, four chiral carbons, and terminal CH2OH, so it is an aldohexose. Note the OH placement on C2, C3, C4, C5 as right-left-right-right. Since the OH on the lowest chiral center is on the right, classify it as a D sugar. Match the R-L-R-R pattern among D-aldohexoses to identify the compound as D-glucose.
